actions.title: Operate the Clean Transport Zone in central Warsaw.
actions.sourceName: Transport UM Warszawa: Clean Transport Zone
actions.sourceExcerpt: The official city transport page states that Warsaw's Clean Transport Zone started on 1 July 2024 and restricts the most polluting vehicles in central districts to improve air quality and health.

actions.title: Develop public transport priority, tram routes, bus lanes, and accessibility upgrades.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Warsaw's Climate Neutrality Action Plan lists development of public transport, including accessibility improvements, new tram routes, bus lanes, electric buses, and the third metro line as transport actions.

actions.title: Build the tram route to Wilanow with street and cycling upgrades.
actions.sourceName: City of Warsaw: Tram Route to Wilanow
actions.sourceExcerpt: The city reported active works on the Wilanow tram corridor, including tracks, shared tram-bus stops, pavements, cycle paths, and underground utility rebuilding.

actions.title: Complete the western M2 metro extension to Lazurowa, Chrzanow, and Karolin.
actions.sourceExcerpt: A May 2026 city update says finishing works are underway on three new Bemowo-side M2 stations and the depot, with surface works adding sidewalks and cycle paths.

actions.title: Expand Warsaw's zero-emission electric bus fleet.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The official city update says MZA expanded its order so Warsaw will add 158 zero-emission buses and expects the electric fleet to exceed 450 vehicles.

actions.title: Retrofit municipal buildings for energy efficiency, PV, and heat pumps.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The city project page describes retrofits of six communal residential buildings with insulation, window and door upgrades, heating modernization, PV, and heat pumps through 30 June 2026.

actions.title: Build new Park and Ride hubs in Rembertow and Brodno.
actions.sourceExcerpt: A May 2026 city update says P+R projects are advancing in Rembertow and Brodno, including EV charging, bike spaces, permeable paving, rainwater retention, and PV with storage.

actions.title: Roll out renewable energy installations across municipal units.
actions.sourceName: Eko UM Warszawa: Municipal renewable energy
actions.sourceExcerpt: Warsaw's climate portal reported more than 500 renewable-energy installations in municipal units, including 413 PV systems, with planned 2022-2030 program funding.

actions.title: Fund onsite rainwater and snowmelt retention systems.
actions.sourceName: Eko UM Warszawa: Rainwater retention grants
actions.sourceExcerpt: The current city page says Warsaw offers grants covering up to 80 percent of costs for onsite rainwater and snowmelt retention systems, including soakaway devices and tanks.

actions.title: Replace obsolete solid-fuel stoves in municipal and private buildings.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Warsaw's official project page says the city removed more than 95 percent of smoky stoves from municipal stock since 2018 and supported private unit replacements.

actions.title: Adapt public transport to climate impacts and expand low-emission service.
actions.sourceName: Krakow Climate Change Adaptation Plan to 2030
actions.sourceExcerpt: Krakow's adaptation plan includes adapting public transport to climate-change impacts, building stop shelters, replacing bus and tram stock with modern low-emission vehicles, and expanding tram infrastructure.

actions.title: Implement the Krakow Clean Transport Zone from 2026.
actions.sourceExcerpt: BIP states that the Clean Transport Zone entered into force on 26 June 2025, applies from 1 January 2026, and covers roughly 60 percent of Krakow.

actions.title: Expand Krakow's MPK electric bus fleet.
actions.sourceExcerpt: MPK says Krakow has 121 electric buses, about 20 percent of the fleet, and plans more zero-emission buses and charging infrastructure.

actions.title: Build the KST IV tram line to Mistrzejowice.
actions.sourceExcerpt: ZDMK reports construction of the KST IV line to Mistrzejowice in a PPP model, with works, tests, and acceptance scheduled before service handover.

actions.title: Operate the Park-e-Bike system linked to Park and Ride hubs.
actions.sourceExcerpt: ZTP describes Park-e-Bike as a free bike-rental system tied to P+R hubs including Czerwone Maki, Kurdwanow, Nowy Biezanow, Maly Plaszow, Gorka Narodowa, and Krowodrza Gorka.

actions.title: Create rain gardens at 15 Krakow schools.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The city says it is procuring design documentation for 15 school rain gardens and has more than PLN 2.1 million in FEnIKS funding for the project.

actions.title: Fund rainwater microretention, bioretention, and green roofs.
actions.sourceExcerpt: BIP states that Krakow runs a 2026 call for rainwater-retention measures including tanks, bioretention, drainage, irrigation systems, and green roofs.

actions.title: Deliver Stop Smog upgrades for low-income single-family homes.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The official city page says the Krakow Stop Smog program covers heat-source replacement, heat-source removal, and thermomodernization in 35 single-family buildings.

actions.title: Thermomodernize Krakow schools with PV and heating upgrades.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Krakow reports 146 thermomodernization investments in education buildings over 20 years, with current work including insulation, window and door upgrades, heating modernization, and rooftop PV.

actions.title: Expand Krakow's urban forest area.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Krakow says forest area grew from 1370.80 ha in 2018 to 1665.61 ha at the start of 2025, nearly 300 ha more, under the city forest-expansion program.

actions.title: Build the Gdansk Poludnie-Wrzeszcz tram line.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The city project page says the new line is 3.75 km plus 0.6 km of modernization, with seven stops, a transfer hub, and a 12-minute trip between Piecki-Migowo and Wrzeszcz.

actions.title: Open the Armii Krajowej bicycle ecostrada corridor.
actions.sourceExcerpt: City news reports Gdansk opened the first stage of the ecostrada along al. Armii Krajowej, about 2 km long, linking Chelm with Srodmiescie.

actions.title: Procure 30 new electric buses for the city fleet.
actions.sourceExcerpt: GAiT says 30 zero-emission electric buses are to join the fleet, with batteries sized for more than 300 km and an investment value over PLN 110 million.

actions.title: Build small-retention sites, rain gardens, and basins.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Gdansk's 2023 city report says Gdanskie Wody built nine small-retention facilities, including rain gardens and four retention basins.

actions.title: Depave urban sites for microretention, biodiversity, and shade.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The official city report says five paved locations were depaved, soil was replaced, and sites were planted with trees, shrubs, grasses, and perennials.

actions.title: Complete the Jaskowa Dolina retention reservoir.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The city report says the Jaskowa Dolina retention reservoir was completed with about 9.3 thousand cubic meters of capacity and recreational surroundings.

actions.title: Upgrade stormwater drainage at Nowe Ogrody and 3 Maja.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Official reporting says Gdansk completed stormwater upgrades at the Nowe Ogrody-3 Maja junction, including storm sewer, chambers, road inlets, and linear drainage.

actions.title: Complete the right flood embankment on the Oplyw Motlawy.
actions.sourceExcerpt: The city report says Gdansk completed the right flood embankment of the Oplyw Motlawy from ul. Elblaska to ul. Zawodnikow to strengthen flood safety.

actions.title: Integrate Port Czystej Energii into the municipal waste and energy system.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Official city material describes Port Czystej Energii as a waste-to-energy CHP plant for non-recyclable residual waste, electricity production, and district heat supply.

actions.title: Replace coal stoves and remove solid-fuel heating in city housing.
actions.sourceExcerpt: Official city reporting says grants supported heating changes and removed 129 traditional coal stoves, while municipal housing work removed 84 solid-fuel hearths.
